absent: Locking, concurrency and lifetime rules for page iterators, mapping iterators and depot records.
Implementation and failure modes of page iterator start and advance helpers.
Mapping iterator map, consume, flush and unmap lifecycle and mapping mode effects.
SipHash and half SipHash core block processing, finalization and test vectors.
Stack depot allocation, lookup, hashing, eviction and RCU reclamation.
Backing engines for bounded copy, user duplication, table matching, unescape and escape.
DMA mapping requirements and cache coherency obligations for DMA walks.
Error codes and boundary behaviour for truncation, padding and case conversion.

findings.text: Scatter-gather page cursor tracks the current entry in sg with the page index inside that entry in sg_pgoffset, plus private controls for remaining entries and step size on the next move. Callers use the first two for position and must leave the private controls opaque.
DMA page cursor contains only an embedded ordinary page cursor as base, so all position state lives in the wrapped cursor and DMA behaviour comes from separate stepping and address helpers.

Two accessors expose cursor position without changing it. The ordinary form yields the kernel page for the current entry and offset. The DMA form yields the DMA address for a DMA cursor by combining the entry DMA base with the in-entry page index scaled to page size.

List walks share a start plus test-advance loop shape. Setup receives a list, a cursor, a count and an initial page skip. The loop condition advances the cursor and reports whether another page remains. A DMA variant applies the same shape to the embedded base with DMA-aware advancement.
Table walks reuse list walks by supplying the table embedded list and a table count. Page walks use the original count while DMA walks use the mapped count, both with a caller supplied initial skip.

Mapping cursor exposes page, addr, length, consumed and an embedded page cursor in piter, together with private offset inside the page, bytes left on the page and option flags. Documentation marks the first group as directly accessible and the second as internal.

Mapping options use low bit positions. Atomic mapping occupies bit zero, writeback to storage occupies bit one, read from storage occupies bit two, and local mapping occupies bit three. The read-from-storage option is documented as having no effect.

Full hash keys store two sixty-four bit words, while half hash keys store two unsigned long words. Alignment follows the natural alignment of the respective word type, and a widened full key spelling requests sixteen byte alignment. A predicate reports whether both words of a full key are zero.

Short inputs are packed before hashing, with two thirty-two bit values forming one sixty-four bit value and four such values forming two sixty-four bit values. Generic hashing selects an unaligned-tolerant path when the build supports efficient unaligned access or when the pointer is misaligned, otherwise an aligned path. The aligned path specializes compile-time-known lengths of four, eight, sixteen, twenty-four and thirty-two bytes into fixed-arity calls, delegating other lengths to a general aligned routine.

Half-size hashing uses the same build plus alignment choice between unaligned and aligned paths. The aligned path specializes compile-time-known lengths of four, eight, twelve and sixteen bytes into fixed-arity thirty-two bit word calls, delegating other lengths to a general aligned routine.

The wide mixing operation combines four state words with adds, exclusive ors and rotations using distances thirteen with thirty-two, sixteen, twenty-one, and seventeen with thirty-two. Its four initialization words are 0x736f6d6570736575, 0x646f72616e646f6d, 0x6c7967656e657261 and 0x7465646279746573. The narrow mixing operation uses the same shape with distances five with sixteen, eight, seven, and thirteen with sixteen, and initialization words 0, 0, 0x6c796765 and 0x74656462.

Integer ordering helper returns a negative, zero or positive result according to whether the left operand is less than, equal to or greater than the right operand, derived arithmetically from the two comparisons.

Depot handles are thirty-two bit values viewed either as opaque handle or as three fields: pool_index_plus_1 carrying a one-biased pool index, offset inside the pool, and extra tag bits. Field widths fill the handle width after reserving offset and extra portions.

Depot records chain with hash_list, store hash and size, carry an immutable handle and a reference count in count, and hold either a fixed frame array in entries or management state. The management overlay holds free_list linkage and an RCU cookie in rcu_state. Records may join the freelist only while the count is zero, and the overlay must not be touched once the record is in use.

Extra tag width is five bits. Pool order is two for a four page pool, with pool size derived from page shift plus pool order. Record alignment is four bytes. Offset width derives from pool order plus page shift minus alignment shift, and pool index width occupies the remaining handle bits after offset and extra.

Depot flags use a thirty-two bit mask type. Allocation permission occupies bit zero and reference acquisition occupies bit one. The interface defines two valid flags with a mask covering the low two bits.
Initialization, early-initialization request and early-initialization entry points are inert in this view, either returning success or doing nothing, so real setup must live outside these fragments.

User array duplication guards against size computation overflow before copying. It checks multiplication of element count by element size and reports an overflow failure without copying when the check fails. Only on success does it forward the computed byte count to the single-buffer user duplication path, with ordinary and vmalloc-backed variants sharing the guard.

Bounded string copying dispatches on call shape. Calls without an explicit size infer it from the destination array, while calls with a size pass it through. Helpers enforce array and string kind expectations at build time. The sized padded variant copies then zero-fills any tail beyond the terminator up to the bound.

Small string utilities trim surrounding whitespace with a must-check result, return the portion after the final separator or the whole input when absent, report prefix length on match and zero otherwise, test prefix and suffix membership with a short-input guard for suffixes, detect all-zero buffers through inverted byte search, and verify presence of a terminator within a bound.

Fixed-buffer moves between byte arrays and strings require build-time-known array sizes and enforce byte-array versus string kind expectations, failing the build otherwise. Copies truncate to fit, string destinations are always terminated, and padded forms fill the unused tail with zeros or a caller-chosen pad byte.

Memory helpers select thirty-two or sixty-four bit filling from the word size, including a pointer-wide form, and provide partial-structure fills from after a member or from a member to the end. Concatenation checks operand type identity at build time. Cache-flushing copy behaves as plain copy here, justified copy ignores its justification, explicit zeroing adds a compiler barrier against elision, duplication forwards through allocation hooks, and sysfs lookup forwards to a sized table matcher.

Boolean-to-word helpers return one of two words per polarity, with inverted spellings negating the input before delegating. Covered oppositions include assertion, enablement, level, direction, power, access, truth, vertical motion and affirmation, for example truth uses true with false and power uses on with off. A plural helper yields empty for a singular count and letter s otherwise.

Unescape wrappers provide in-place operation and any-class decoding by defaulting flags and buffers before delegating to the general unescape engine. Escape wrappers default to escaping plus non-printable handling for memory and string inputs before delegating to the general escape engine. Case helpers convert null-terminated strings to upper or lower case including the terminator.

Unescape classes occupy bits zero through three for space, octal, hexadecimal and special forms, with a combined any form and a mask over those bits. Escape classes occupy bits zero through eight for space, special, null, octal, non-printable, hexadecimal, two extra selectors and an append mode, with combined any forms and a mask over all bits. Size formatting selects decimal or binary units in a low bit and offers high-bit modifiers to suppress spacing and the byte suffix.

Name hashing starts from a caller salt, mixes each character with shifts by four, addition and multiplication by eleven, and finalizes through a long-hash fold to thirty-two bits. A packed value stores length in the high thirty-two bits and hash in the low thirty-two bits with accessors and a constructor. Stringification expands arguments before quoting, and a file-line helper combines the file name with the expanded line number.
